_comment: THE URL TRANSITION MAP — every currently public route, and what happens
to it when Indo-Pacific Record launches.
It is data rather than code because it is a promise about a published
surface, and a promise has to be checkable. Tests read this file, compare
it against what output/ actually holds, and against what the candidate
build actually emits. A route that exists in production and is missing
NOTHING HERE IS DEPLOYED BY THIS BRANCH. No redirect is written to the
live site, no DNS record is changed, and no domain is selected. This is
the plan the launch executes, pinned so it cannot drift before then.

dispositions.preserve: The route keeps working at the same URL. Its content may change; its address does not.
dispositions.move: The route moves. The old address keeps resolving via a redirect that names exactly one new address.
dispositions.legacy_archive: Preserved as published, under an explicit legacy label. Not rewritten to look as though it appeared under the new name.
dispositions.owner_decision: Retired only with owner approval. Nothing on this branch removes it.
dispositions.evidence: Never deleted. It is cited, or it is the record of a citation.

routes.note: The home page keeps its address and gets the regional masthead and the desk directory.
Same page as /, addressed explicitly.

The record index. Deliberately NOT renamed to /records.html: this is a live public address, and the navigation label can change without the URL changing. 'Record' in navigation, /archive.html on the wire.
Keeps its address; gains the regional scope statement and the derived corpus metrics.
'Signals & Methodology' has no separate equivalent in the regional model — its content is methodology. One redirect to one page; it is not folded into the home page.

Every published article URL keeps resolving, each to the record page holding the same article. Redirects are generated from the corpus, never from a directory listing, so an id absent from the snapshot acquires no redirect to nothing. Mass-redirecting these to the home page is forbidden: they are cited.
The weekly series index, published under the predecessor masthead. Preserved as published.
Same page as /the-pla-watch/, addressed explicitly.
The full edition archive. The candidate links to it rather than copying it.
Thirteen published editions. Issue numbers, titles, deks, bylines and dates are unchanged, and none is rewritten to appear as though it were published under the new name.
The canonical edition record each rendered page is generated from. Never hand-edited, never deleted.
The series glossary, as published.
Subscribers hold this address. Moving a feed silently unsubscribes everyone who did not notice.
Edition cover images, referenced by the published pages.
Media referenced by the published editions.
Repository plumbing that happens to be deployed. Harmless, and removing it is not this transition's business.

Editorial imagery for the predecessor identity. The regional design uses no stock or platform photography, so these become unreferenced at launch — but they are referenced by published pages until then, and removal is an owner decision, not a side effect.

An existing machine-readable export. The candidate publishes /corpus-index.json instead, which is a different shape. Keeping both, retiring this one, or redirecting it is an owner decision; nothing here removes it.
Predecessor mark. The candidate ships /mark.svg; which file the launch serves as the favicon is a deployment decision.
Predecessor mark, referenced by published edition pages. Not removed here.
Predecessor wordmark, referenced by published edition pages. Not removed here.
Social preview image carrying the predecessor identity. Replacing it is part of the launch, not of this candidate.
Regenerated at launch with whatever sitemap address the launch uses.
Regenerated at launch. It must list the new addresses, not the redirects.
The deployed domain. Domain selection and DNS are owner decisions and are explicitly outside this branch.
